page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB per vCPU, and includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in memory-intensive and single-threaded operations. The server achieves a strong read-only large-block memory bandwidth of 181.85 GB/sec, though its Passmark memory score falls in the lower 25th percentile. Computational performance is highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and a multi-core score of 16603.0, both ranking in the top 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 31.08 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput is measured at 43.34 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference achieves 296.69 tokens/sec for text generation on small 135M models, but drops to a poor 2.45 tokens/sec on large 70B models, demonstrating a clear performance tradeoff for large-scale AI tasks without dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E64-32ds_v6 offers high memory density and bundled local storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for data-intensive operations. The combination of 512.0 GB of RAM, dedicated high-frequency Intel Xeon cores, and fast local NVMe storage makes this instance highly suitable for memory-heavy workloads. Recommended applications include large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, data analytics pipelines, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and web serving environments requiring high throughput.
